target_customer: Protein design teams at biotech companies, pharma and universities that need fast wet lab validation of designed proteins
problem: Testing designed proteins in the lab is slow and expensive and limits how fast AI protein design can iterate. Adaptyv offers automated lab testing by API and web order.
business_model: Lab as a service, per protein assay fees (listed from 149 USD per protein) plus data products
product_category: Automated protein engineering lab and validation service

founders.name: Julian Englert
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as Protein Data Dealer with no bio.

founders.name: Daniel Nakhaee-Zadeh Gutierrez
education: Experience developed at Harvard, University of Leeds, KAIST and EPFL (degrees not stated on YC page)
founders.background_notes: YC page describes immunoengineering, synthetic biology and computational biology work.

founders.name: Amir Shahein
founders.background_notes: Named as a founder by Biopole; background not stated.

founders.name: Moustafa Houmani
founders.background_notes: Named as a founder by Biopole; background not stated.

technical_complexity.rationale: Combines cell free synthesis, nanofluidics, lab robotics and software into an automated protein foundry; the 2023 launch article describes lab-on-chip work cells meant to replace several commercial instruments.

defensibility.rationale: Hardware and process know-how plus accumulating protein assay data are hard to replicate quickly, but wet lab validation services are a contestable market.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent acquisition or copy was found in sources opened; the company raised a 40M Series A in 2026.

market_need_then: Generative AI protein design was emerging in 2021 and made experimental validation the bottleneck; the 2023 launch article calls conventional testing slow, costly and failure prone.

branding.domain_note: Uses adaptyvbio.com, not an exact adaptyv.com.

identity.voice_and_tone: technical and confident, claims of being the fastest protein validation lab

branding.brand_signature: Anthropic x Adaptyv protein design competition and logo wall of AI protein design teams on the site

rebrands.why: Sources use both names interchangeably; no sourced rebrand event, date unknown

branding.community_and_virality: Company site lists a design competition and case study with Anthropic; no independent fan or merch evidence found.

brand_strength.rationale: Recognized among protein design teams per the site's customer logos, but evidence is mostly company-published.

outcome_analysis: Adaptyv is active and growing: a CHF 2.5 million pre-seed in February 2022, an 8 million dollar seed in 2025 and a 40 million dollar Series A in August 2026. It rode the rise of AI protein design, which created demand for fast wet lab data, and now sells to well known AI and pharma teams.
notes: Pre-seed amount is CHF 2.5 million per Biopole; USD amount not stated so left null (an aggregator says 2.5 million USD, unverified). Seed date varies: Biopole article 2025-09 says completed earlier in 2025, an aggregator says October 2025 or November 2024. Series A lead and amount come from raising.fi and the company site headline, with the company blog dated 2026-08-25. Competition: no competitor source dated near mid 2021 was found; CB Insights lists Turbine, Biomatter, Arzeda, 64x Bio and Cradle without dates, so none are recorded. Competitors list left empty for that reason. Founder CEO and CTO titles come from aggregators only. No shutdown or layoff news found.
